citation: "The Old Kinzie House (First House Built in Chicago)" — colour postcard after a painting, "By Courtesy of John H. Kinzie", Curt Teich & Co., Chicago, about 1910.
author: unidentified painter; printed by Curt Teich & Co.
date: about 1910 (the postcard); the painting's date is not recorded
describes_date: the house under the Kinzies, before it was given up in the early 1830s; the card names no year
repository: Newberry Library, Curt Teich Postcard Archives (NBY 416153), via Wikimedia Commons; the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_kinzie_house_1804.jpg (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md)
locator: the whole card, 960 x 609 px in the copy held here; the title is lettered at top left and the courtesy line at bottom left
rights_note: Published before 1930 in the United States; the Newberry's scan is offered on Commons as public domain.
access_notes: Read off the image file itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2498). Whether John H. Kinzie (1803-1865) lent the painting itself or a copy of it is not stated on the card.
what_it_supplies: the only picture of the house in colour: a red-brown roof and cream walls under the piazza
the west gable broad, with a small square light high in it
two stacks through the ridge, the second toward the east end
the piazza across the front, its roof carried down from the main roof, with a low paling along it
a central door with openings either side
four poplars in a row east of the house running down toward the river, a fenced green, and a great tree behind
what_it_does_not_supply: a date: the card's file name here says 1804 and the card itself says no year
any dimension or position; its colours are a painter's and a printer's, not evidence of 1812
note: A painting of uncertain date reproduced about a century later. It is the one picture that shows a light in a gable, which the 1857 engraving and the Cram plate may also hint at. Its camera and match record are data/reference_views/kinzie_house_1812/teich_postcard.json.
